label.purpose: Panel section headers — the app's dominant micro-pattern.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Popups, dropdowns, tooltips — anything floating above the page.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Input focus state, paired with an accent-tinted border.

motion.name: ease-house
motion.purpose: Canonical easing for every entrance/exit outside the auth screens: fade-ups, modal/popup entrances, tab transitions. Never use an overshoot (back-out) curve outside auth.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one primary action per screen (Scan Now, + Add Vendor).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--accent, #8B5CF6); color: #fff; border: none; border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px 16px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--accent-h, #7C3AED); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent-l, #A78BFA); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.05); color: var(--mid, #B4B6C2); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.08); border-radius: 8px; padding: 8px 16px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms, color 150ms; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.08); color: var(--hi, #F5F6FA); }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Text input with label, used in forms (Add Vendor, notes composer).
components.css: .ds-field-label { display: block; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--mid, #B4B6C2); margin-bottom: 6px; } .ds-input { width: 100%; background: var(--elevated, #1C1D24); border: 1px solid var(--line, #23242C); border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px 16px; font-size: 14px; color: var(--hi, #F5F6FA); outline: none; transition: border-color 150ms, box-shadow 150ms; } .ds-input:focus { border-color: rgba(139,92,246,0.5); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(139,92,246,0.1); }

components.name: Panel / Card
components.description: The base container for every content section — flat, hairline border, no shadow.
components.css: .ds-panel { background: var(--surface, #15161C); border: 1px solid var(--line, #23242C); border-radius: 12px; padding: 24px; } .ds-panel-title { font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--hi, #F5F6FA); margin-bottom: 16px; }

components.name: Select Trigger + Listbox
components.description: Themed combobox replacing native <select> — see components/Select.jsx. Popup shown open for reference; in practice it's portaled to document.body and positioned via getBoundingClientRect.
components.html:
Financial / Payment — 1.6×
Authentication / SSO — 1.6×
components.css: .ds-select-trigger { width: 100%; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 8px; background: var(--elevated, #1C1D24); border: 1px solid var(--accent, #8B5CF6); border-radius: 8px; padding: 10px 12px; font-size: 12px; color: var(--hi, #F5F6FA); cursor: pointer; } .ds-chevron { color: var(--lo, #8A8C98); transform: rotate(180deg); transition: transform 150ms; } .ds-listbox { margin-top: 6px; background: var(--elevated, #1C1D24); border: 1px solid var(--border, #2A2B34); border-radius: 12px; padding: 6px 0; box-shadow: 0 12px 40px rgba(0,0,0,0.7); font-size: 12px; } .ds-option { padding: 8px 12px; color: var(--hi, #F5F6FA); cursor: pointer; } .ds-option--active { background: rgba(139,92,246,0.15); color: var(--accent-l, #A78BFA); }

components.name: Tabs
components.css: .ds-tablist { display: flex; gap: 6px; padding: 4px; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.03); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.05); border-radius: 12px; width: fit-content; } .ds-tab { padding: 6px 14px; border-radius: 8px; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; background: transparent; color: var(--lo, #8A8C98); border: none; cursor: pointer; transition: color 150ms, background 150ms; } .ds-tab:hover { color: var(--mid, #B4B6C2); } .ds-tab--active { background: rgba(139,92,246,0.15); color: var(--accent-l, #A78BFA); }

components.name: Risk Badge
components.description: Dot + label risk indicator, the app's most-repeated semantic element.
components.css: .ds-risk-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 5px; padding: 4px 10px; border-radius: 9999px; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.02em; } .ds-risk-badge--high { background: rgba(240,68,56,0.12); color: #FCA5A5; } .ds-risk-dot { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background: #F04438; flex-shrink: 0; }

narrative.overview: VenderScope's real identity is the dashboard and vendor-detail screens: dense, sober, quiet, built for a GRC/InfoSec analyst who opens it daily and needs to trust what it says at a glance. Dark, near-black surfaces; a single violet accent used sparingly; small confident type; hairline borders instead of shadows. Nothing decorative competes with the data. The auth screens (Login, Register, Guest Scan) are a deliberate, confirmed exception — a consumer-SaaS-register first-impression moment that the 2026-08-25 design critique found tonally distinct from the rest of the app, and the product owner chose to keep as-is rather than converge. This split is intentional, not drift.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black surfaces with a single violet accent (#8B5CF6), used on ≤10% of any given screen
Flat by default — hairline borders separate surfaces, not shadows
Small, confident type (11–14px body/labels); large tabular-nums reserved for risk scores only
One house motion curve (cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)) everywhere except the auth screens' own register
Auth screens are the one confirmed exception to all of the above

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Violet is the only non-semantic color in the system. If a new element needs emphasis and isn't communicating risk, it's violet or it's neutral — never a new arbitrary color.

rules.name: The Risk Vocabulary Is Closed Rule
rules.body: Red/amber/green mean vendor/event risk and nothing else. Toast borrowing risk-high red for error chrome is the one sanctioned exception, because a failed action genuinely is a risk signal in this product.

rules.name: The Uppercase Label Rule
rules.body: Any section header inside a panel is a small (10–11px), bold, wide-tracked, uppercase label in text-lo. The single most repeated typographic pattern in the app.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: If it's not currently floating above the page (modal, popup, dropdown, tooltip), it does not get a box-shadow. Reach for a border or a background-tint step instead.

dos: Do use the house motion curve cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) for every entrance/exit outside the auth screens' own register

Do portal any popup/overlay positioned fixed that sits inside an ancestor with a persistent transform (Panel's fade-up ... both leaves transform: translateY(0) applied forever) — Select.jsx and EventFeed.jsx's AcceptedBadge are the reference implementations
Do keep DOM focus on a control's trigger for any custom listbox/menu/combobox; track the active item via aria-activedescendant, never by moving focus into the popup
Do exempt in-progress indicators (spinners, skeletons) from the global prefers-reduced-motion freeze — a frozen spinner during a multi-minute operation reads as a hung app
Do treat the auth screens as the one confirmed exception to this document's sober instrument-panel register
donts: Don't use a native <select> for anything the user needs to read against this theme — its option popup is OS-rendered and no CSS reaches it. Use components/Select.jsx
Don't unmount a tab panel or any container that might hold in-progress user input on visibility toggle — hide it, state must survive a round-trip
Don't introduce a second red, amber, or green outside the risk-semantic set for anything unrelated to vendor/event risk
Don't add a box-shadow to anything at rest
Don't reach for an overshoot/back-out easing curve outside the auth screens — it reads as consumer-SaaS bounce, precisely the register the dashboard is not
Don't silently swallow an error in a catch block with only console.error, or omit the catch entirely, on any user-triggered action — every failure must surface visibly
